newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania-Hungary relations to start new era-minister.
newsitem.headline: Romania-Hungary relations to start new era-minister.

text.p: Relations between Romania and Hungary will get off to a fresh start under their new treaty, Romanian Foreign Minister Adrian Severin said on Thursday.

"The Romanian-Hungarian partnership is one of the most important elements of stability in the region," Severin told Reuters as he prepared for a three-day visit to Hungary to exchange ratification documents for the treaty.
"We want to start something new with Hungary. "I am confident ties between Romania and Hungary will enter a new era."

The pact, signed in September, is vital to the ambition of Romania and Hungary to move closer to Europe and NATO. It aims to end old quarrels by guaranteeing Romania's western borders and ensuring the rights of Romania's 1.6 million ethnic Hungarians.

Ties between Budapest and Bucharest had long been tense, mainly because of disputes over the status of ethnic Hungarians and because Romanian nationalists suspected Budapest of designs on Transylvania, once ruled by Austro-Hungary.

Since the fall of communism in 1989, Romania's ethnic Hungarians had tried to improve their standing but their demands for more rights met stiff opposition from the former leftist cabinet, which included nationalist parties.
Victory by centrist parties in November polls and the inclusion of ethnic Hungarians in the new government -- a first in post-communist Romania -- brought a change of mood.
Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said his cabinet would "openly" cooperate with the government in Budapest.

"We have to focus on what connects, not what separates, Romania and Hungary, although history has burdened Romanian- Hungarian relations with problems and tragic events," newly elected President Emil Constantinescu said recently.
Severin's visit will be his first official trip since he took office this month.

He will meet President Arpad Goncz, Prime Minister Gyula Horn and Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs, plus members of the right-wing opposition who opposed ratification of the treaty, saying it still failed to guarantee sufficient rights for Romania's ethnic Hungarians.
"It's a must to meet those politicians. Nothing can replace dialogue," Severin said.
